{{nihongo|'''Tomari Shrine'''|泊神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

'''Tomari Shrine''' (とまりじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} on {{ill|Shikine-jima|Q1344326|qid=Q1344326}}, southwest of {{ill|Niijima, Tokyo|Q1204534|qid=Q1204534}}, {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}.

It is identified with '''Kunitsuhime-no-Mikoto Shrine''' (くにつひめのみことじんじゃ), a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}<ref name="yao">[https://yaokami.jp/1131744/ 泊神社] - Yaoyorozu no Kami</ref>.

=== Overview ===
Its founding is unknown, but as it is identified with a Shikinaisha, its origin goes back to at least ancient times.

In {{ill|1912|Q2077|qid=Q2077}} (Meiji 45), it was moved to the current site while enshrining other deities together<ref name="kanko">[https://shikinejima.tokyo/learn/historic/historic_place/1062/ 泊神社] - Shikinejima Tourism Association</ref>.

The name "Tomari Shrine" began to be used in {{ill|1953|Q18585|qid=Q18585}} (Shōwa 28), and from {{ill|1960|Q3754|qid=Q3754}} (Shōwa 35) onward repairs to the worship hall and new construction of a kagura hall were carried out step by step, forming its present layout<ref name="kanko"/>.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* Tomari Mitokuchi Ōkisaki Myōjin (みとのくち おおきさきみょうじん) - Kunitsuhime-no-Mikoto, consort of {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611}}<ref name="yao"/><ref name="kanko"/>.
